1. Open the starwars dataset (located in tidyverse)
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
data(starwars)
```

2. Create a scatter plot of character's height and mass.
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass)) + geom_point()

```

2a. Change the color and shape of the points in your scatter plot. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass)) + geom_point(shape = 3, color = "darkorchid4") 
```

3. Add Homeworld as a third variable to your scatterplot. 
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass, color = homeworld)) + geom_point(shape = 3)

```

3a. What do you notice about the graph? (e.g. describe what you see)
#The graph contains a very large legend as there are several homeworlds. It is colored with an automatic pallette of colors that are very similar to each other. It is difficult to decipher trends in height and weight based on this graph as the legend is so large.
4. Make a boxplot of height. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(y=height))+geom_boxplot()

```

5. Make a boxplot of height for each species present in the data. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, species))+geom_boxplot()

```

5a. change the appearance of your graph in at least 3 ways. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, species))+geom_boxplot(fill = "pink", color="darkorchid")+ xlab("Height")+ylab("Species")+ggtitle("Height of Star Wars Characters by Species")
```

6. Using any variables in the starwars dataset, create a graph that uses a color palette from viridis.
```{r}
install.packages("viridis")
library(viridis)

ggplot(starwars, aes(height, fill = sex))+geom_histogram()+scale_fill_viridis(option = "magma", discrete = TRUE)
```

7.Using any variables in the starwars dataset, create a graph that uses a color palette from RColorBrewer.
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass, color = gender))+geom_point(na.rm = TRUE)+scale_color_brewer(palette = "Oranges", direction = -1)

```

8. Using any variables in the starwars dataset, create a graph using facet_wrap
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass))+geom_boxplot()+facet_wrap(~gender)

```
